_readme: WHICH play route has a GAME BOARD, and what ARIA role its cells declare. Keyed route -> the
cell's class selector and the role authored on it. gh#214, owner ruling 2026-09-10.
WHY A REGISTRY AT ALL, and what it is NOT. The 2026-09-10 ruling forbids the GATE keying its
exemption off a hand-maintained list of routes or selectors: the gate reads the role off the live
DOM and stays list-free. This file is the other half and a different thing — only a human can say
which grid is a BOARD. Eleven routes carry `display: grid` in their own CSS or engine and ten of
them are ordinary grid-laid-out panels: a keypad, a stepper, a roster, an avatar picker. No
detector can tell a 12-key numpad from a 25-stone board, because geometrically they are the same
thing. So this file AUTHORS the judgement, the route's own module authors the role onto the DOM,
and scripts/control-floor-probe.mjs reads the role back off the rendered page.
WHAT THE PROBE USES IT FOR, and it is one thing: the anti-vacuity leg the ruling names. An
exemption keyed on a role greens on the empty set if the cells never declare that role, and a
gate that exempts by role and finds no roles prints the same green as a gate that checked and
passed. So every route listed here must yield at least one measured control matching `cell` AND
declaring `cellRole`, or the probe FAILS. Both fields are load-bearing: rename the class or drop
the role and that leg reds on the day it lands.
WHERE THE ROLE IS AUTHORED. Not here, and not in markup.html / style.css / main.js — those three
are rewritten byte-for-byte from the mockup by scripts/extract-mockup.mjs, so an attribute typed
into any of them is undone by the next extraction (the same problem src/play/_aria-labels.json
exists to solve for accessible names). one-bomb's board is built entirely in its repo-authored
main.ts, which the extractor does NOT write, so the role survives re-extraction by construction
rather than by a re-apply pass.
ponytail: a board built in an extractor-owned main.js has NO re-apply path today, and there is no
such board to build one for. The upgrade path when one ships is the injector idiom already in
scripts/play-aria-labels.mjs — a role stamped into the extractor's output from this table, called
from extract-mockup.mjs beside applyLabels.
THE COST THE OWNER ACCEPTED, recorded because it is real and player-facing: `role=grid` announces
a grid widget, and a grid widget is expected to answer arrow keys with a roving tabindex. This
board does not — every stone is a real <button> in tab order. And `gridcell` on a <button>
element is outside the roles ARIA-in-HTML advises for that element, so a screen reader announces
a cell where it used to announce a button. Both were shown to the owner with the ruling that
authored these roles. The upgrade path is arrow-key navigation on the board, not removing them.

one-bomb.why: The stones of the no-3D board: one <button> per cell of a rows x cols grid sized from the seat count. A tap on one IS the move and the board is the route's whole play surface, which is what makes these cells rather than an ordinary grid-laid-out panel. Measured in this walk at 56.796875px square on the two-seat default board.
